publications.title: K HEADS IS ALL YOU NEED: TASK-DEPENDENT CIRCUIT GRANULARITY AND ZERO-TRAINING ROUTING IN LLMS
publications.abstract:
I show that a single computational behavior – needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) retrieval in Qwen2.5-1.5B – is supported by a causal circuit of just six attention heads, sufficient to recover the behavior under isolation and necessary under knockout, validated against layer-matched random controls rather than raw ablation deltas. The same six-head class of circuit recovers NIAH-MultiKey retrieval with minor expansion, and a five-head compression produces a 100% causal steering flip on a counterfactual retrieval target.

I test whether transformer computation is generally this sparse across counting, sorting, variable tracking, and Python synthesis primitives using the identical causal validation protocol (JCCS greedy ACDC + CoAx specificity tagging). The boundary is structured: sparse for retrieval, dense for reasoning and variable tracking. Across Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B, Llama-3.2-1B, and Gemma-2-2B, a zero-training Layer-4 cosine gate detects compressible inputs at inference time with zero false activations on 100 out-of-distribution RULER 4K prompts.

publications.title: THE SHAPE OF COMPUTATION: LANGUAGE MODELS BUILD UNIVERSAL, CONSERVED TASK GEOMETRIES THAT ARE CAUSALLY INERT
publications.abstract:
Using train/test-separated PCA, layer-wise F-statistics, and CKA-aligned dynamic time warping (DTW across 720 label permutations, p ≈ 0.00139, replicated three times) after removing template leakage, we show that task representations follow a conserved trunk-and-branch geometry across models of different widths and depths.

Under contrastive activation steering with magnitude-matched random controls, causal efficacy fails to track geometric maturation (r = 0.049 and r = 0.112 against a pre-registered bar of r > 0.7). Dual-metric trajectory attribution reveals MLPs construct this geometry almost entirely while attention heads oppose it — establishing that language models construct a real, universal geometric map of task identity that is epiphenomenal rather than causally sufficient.

publications.title: NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: CONVERGENT COMPUTATIONAL GEOMETRY IN THE TRANSFORMER RESIDUAL STREAM
publications.abstract:
Tests and explicitly falsifies the fixed hardware-like Head ISA hypothesis across 12 ablation phases (held-out recall collapses: WRITE = 0.311, LOAD = 0.079). Shifting to representation space, after regressing out five lexical and difficulty confounds via OLS across Qwen2.5, Llama-3.2, and Phi-1.5, deconfounded operational geometry is conserved cross-architecture (Mantel p < 0.003; ρ = 0.9644) and identifies the Intersection Circuit.

Causal ablation confirms these residual directions are necessary (removing a category's direction selectively collapses its task), yet additive steering and substitution fail to render them sufficient elsewhere — defining the necessity-without-sufficiency gap.

publications.title: The HeadGenome Taxonomy: A Structural and Causal Map of Attention Head Specialization in Transformers
publications.abstract:
Classifies 1,568 attention heads across four architectures (GPT-2 Medium, Qwen-2.5-0.5B/1.5B, Llama-3.2-1B) into Sink, Local, Retrieval, and Induction classes via a dynamic entropy-collapse probe, proving static SVD weight clustering is functionally blind. Establishes a depth scaling law for Frobenius ratio ∥W_V∥_F / ∥W_Q∥_F (p = 1.92 × 10⁻¹²⁷), an Early/Late Induction split (p = 4.17 × 10⁻³²), and contrasts trained vs. random-covariance SAEs (L₀ = 4.57 vs. 51.07).

Exposes a perplexity illusion (13.07 vs. 11.71 perplexity masking a 100% → 42% retrieval collapse), yields 13.3× KV compression over StreamingLLM, and achieves 1.92× (4K) to 2.81× (8K) FlexAttention speedup.

publications.title: O(1) Decode Step Attention for Any Transformer via Training-Free Proactive KV Cache Eviction
publications.abstract:
Replaces reactive KV-cache eviction (StreamingLLM, H2O) with offline head-pattern prototype clustering and a lightweight TF-IDF ingest predictor that bounds cached keys to a fixed budget B regardless of context length — giving O(B²) = O(1) decode attention per token with zero fine-tuning.

On WikiText-103 (budget 256), achieves PPL 76.8 vs. StreamingLLM (152.7) and H2O (220.2); on PG-19 (~70K tokens, budget 128), PPL 77.4; and on LLaMA 3.1 8B (budget 512), achieves PPL 10.25 vs. StreamingLLM 47.34 (4.6× improvement) with a 3.09× decode speedup at 2048-token context.

publications.title: Trinetra: O(N) Video Ingest, O(1) Query — A Proactive Temporal Event Graph for Long-Form Video Understanding
publications.abstract:
Replaces quadratic O(T²) per-query video frame re-processing with a proactive Temporal Event Graph (TEG), Multi-Scale Temporal Attention Shift (TAS2, TAS8, TAS32), and dual FAISS semantic-temporal indexing.

Ingests long-form video once in O(N) linear time and resolves subsequent queries in O(1) graph lookup — demonstrating 9× temporal awareness improvement, 317,500× fewer query-time FLOPs, and 70% clean output vs. 20% for static attention on 20-minute video ablations.
